Hi Alice —

Thanks for the questionnaire. Below are the focused answers for the controls you flagged and attachments we're providing via a secure bucket (links below). I kept the responses terse so your team can slot them into the SIG workbook; we'll also upload a filled spreadsheet by EOD Tue (May 4 CET).

Quick executive summary
- Residency: For hosted (Redwood API) customers, EU data is processed in our eu-central-1 region (single-tenant model routing available for sensitive workloads). For Redwood Private deployments, customers can host the control plane in their VPC or our EU-managed Private control plane; customer data and inference payloads remain in customer-controlled subnets unless they opt into cross-region replication.
- VPC / Private deployments: Private (VPC) deployments are deployed into customer-owned VPCs via PrivateLink or a dedicated peering configuration. There is zero direct cross-tenant routing: compute nodes for Private deployments are bound to tenant-specific subnets and IAM policies restrict management-plane access to Redwood operator accounts with just-in-time access. Management plane telemetry is sampled and forwarded to a separate management VPC with strict egress controls; we do not inject customer inference data into the management telemetry stream.
- KMS / Key handling: For Private and Dedicated offerings we provide two options: (1) Customer-managed keys (CMK) in their AWS KMS, with envelope encryption by Redwood services (recommended) or (2) Redwood-managed keys with tenant key separation in an HSM-backed KMS hosted in EU regions. We can provide an HSM attest packet under NDA. Key material for CMK never leaves the customer's KMS and the envelope keys are rotated monthly.
- Logs & retention: Inference request logs are retained per-customer in a configurable S3 bucket (default 30 days). Customers can set retention to 0 days. Access to raw inference payload logs requires an elevated support request and is audited — no support engineer can access payloads without a documented justification and supervisor approval.

Attachments we will share (secure links below):
- redwood_sig_answers_20270429.xlsx (completed SIG/CAIQ answers; highlighted rows show where we added region-specific notes)
- SOC2-TypeII-2026.pdf (attestation and scope notes)
- privatelink_architecture_v2.png (diagram showing PrivateLink peering, management plane separation, and KMS flow)

Technical notes (short):
- Network isolation: compute plane instances are launched in tenant-specific subnets. Security groups are restrictive by default; we strongly recommend use of PrivateLink + VPC endpoints for customer-to-redwood control-plane communication.
- Management plane: uses a separate VPC with transit gateway peering for operator access; no egress from compute plane to management plane except metrics metadata (no payloads).
- Egress policy / region binding: We support region-binding controls; outbound egress endpoints default to region-local NAT gateways in EU regions. Cross-region failover requires explicit customer opt-in.

- https://redwood-secure.s3.amazonaws.com/healthwave/SOC2-TypeII-2026.pdf
